reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes joining BitConnect, funding an account with Bitcoin, buying BCC, and placing the resulting amount into an investment. It pairs these explicit funding instructions with unusually high projected returns, including a stated 307% return and high or potentially guaranteed interest. the available video evidence describes promotional solicitation and does not claim that transactions, payouts, or losses were completed.

citations.quote: Join Bitconnect: http://www.bit.ly/cryptoyt
you just need to copy this bitcoin address go to your wallet and deposit maybe even just $100 into it
you need to buy BCC
So you will make 370$ profit with this invesment of 299 days.

opening.argument: Judge the earnings discussion as a conditional calculation, not a promise of a fixed payout. The speaker introduces it with “let's say you have one hundred dollars in investment” and bases the rate on “the last 30 days” (ASR_0003). He also describes the smaller purchase amount as something that will “probably” appear in a wallet (ASR_0003). Those qualifications matter: a worked example using a historical rate does not itself establish that future interest is certain or that anyone received the projected amount.

citations.quote: So let's say you have one hundred dollars in investment. The rate of interest for the last 30 days was one point zero three
it will probably be 0.5 BitConnect coins or something in your wallet

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening identifies a join link, funding steps, and a profit figure, but those points do not prove the figure was guaranteed or paid. The speaker explicitly frames the calculation around a hypothetical amount and a historical rate (ASR_0003). The absence of completed payouts or losses in the available account leaves the asserted outcome unverified.

citations.quote: So let's say you have one hundred dollars in investment. The rate of interest for the last 30 days was one point zero three

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Conditional inputs do not make this merely market commentary. The speaker tells viewers to deposit Bitcoin (ASR_0002), buy BCC (ASR_0003), and then presents the resulting investment as profit with a stated 307% return (ASR_0004). No completed payout is needed to recognize the solicitation and its projected earnings.

citations.quote: go to your wallet and deposit maybe even just $100 into it

opening.argument: This is structured as an operational walkthrough: registration and email activation (ASR_0001), browser verification (ASR_0002), and an explanation of where the exchange controls are (ASR_0003). Even at the funding step, the speaker directs viewers who lack a wallet to a separate explanation of how to create one and buy Bitcoin (ASR_0002). A tutorial can show how an investment interface works and calculate an example without establishing that the presenter completed an investment or that a viewer obtained the illustrated returns.

citations.quote: then it's going to say thank you for registering please check your email for instructions to activate your account

if you don't have one i have a video explaining how to make a bitcoin wallet and how to buy bitcoin!

rebuttal.rebuttal: The cited deposit and BCC-purchase instructions are real, but they are also the steps an interface tutorial would have to explain. The speaker introduces the funding amount as an example (ASR_0002), and the opening itself acknowledges that no completed transactions or payouts are established. The profit calculation alone does not show that this walkthrough produced those returns.

citations.quote: So let's say you want to invest a small hundred dollars

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The walkthrough is not detached instruction. Its description says “Join Bitconnect” (DESCRIPTION_0001); the speaker directs viewers to deposit from their own wallets (ASR_0002), buy BCC (ASR_0003), and invest while describing a 307% return (ASR_0004). Whether anyone followed through is separate from what the video promotes.

citations.quote: Join Bitconnect: http://www.bit.ly/cryptoyt
go to your wallet and deposit maybe even just $100 into it
you need to buy BCC
Return of investment of ofcourse 307%

opening.argument: The description includes an ordinary promotional offer: a code for a 3% discount on Genesis Mining (DESCRIPTION_0001). The account setup also includes email activation (ASR_0001) and a browser-verification step described as a safety precaution (ASR_0002). The cited material does not show the presenter collecting viewers' credentials or receiving their Bitcoin; the deposit instruction points viewers to an address within the demonstrated account flow (ASR_0002). Those omissions matter when assessing whether the video itself documents theft, rather than promotion of a third-party service.

citations.quote: Use the code '8VxCBA' and get a 3% discount on Genesis Mining!

It's just safety precaution.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The opening's join link and funding instructions support promotion, but they do not show that the presenter took custody of a viewer's funds or that the projected payout failed. The separate discount code (DESCRIPTION_0001) also shows conventional promotional material alongside the walkthrough. The question is what this evidence establishes, not whether every advertised return should be trusted.

citations.quote: Use the code '8VxCBA' and get a 3% discount on Genesis Mining!

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A discount for Genesis Mining does not explain away the BitConnect investment pitch. The description explicitly invites viewers to join BitConnect (DESCRIPTION_0001), and the speaker instructs them to deposit Bitcoin (ASR_0002), buy BCC (ASR_0003), and expect a calculated profit (ASR_0004). The concern is promotional solicitation around projected investment returns; proof that the presenter personally stole funds is not required.
